event: Nala kneels by each of the six in turn and cuts the core from under the breastbone, as Wren does.
Six small cores, sticky and dark. She wipes them on the grass and bags them with the ears.
Then she goes up the trail, slow, toward the smell of smoke, her sense spreading wide every while.
The cleft ends. The trail climbs on through oak and yew, deeper than she has ever been.
A mile and more on, between one reach and the next, a dry stick cracks loud under her boot.
Twenty paces ahead, two goblins rise from behind a fallen trunk beside the trail. Watchers.
For a heartbeat they stare at her. Then the smaller one turns and bolts up the trail toward camp.
The other snatches a horn from its belt and lifts it to its lips, drawing breath.
